claims.quote: Black ends it a pawn up
claims.why: White is a pawn up now (8 pawns to 7) and Black nets one pawn in the Bd3 line, so material is level at its end.

claims.quote: Black wins a bishop on e3 in that line
claims.why: The line stops on 14...Nxe3 and White recaptures with fxe3, so it is a knight-for-bishop trade, not a bishop won.

claims.quote: off the d-file, which removes any rook or knight checks
claims.why: After Ke2 Black still has the rook check ...Re3+, and the engine's own Ke2 line has the knight check ...Nc3+ against the king on e2.

claims.quote: forces the Black king to recapture
claims.why: After Rxg6+ Black can also play fxg6, Kh7, Kh8 or Kf8, so the king recapture is not forced.

claims.quote: White ends one pawn ahead
claims.why: Black is a pawn up now (8 pawns to 7), so after White nets one pawn in the line material is level, not White a pawn ahead.

claims.quote: It is supported by the rook on b1
claims.why: A rook on b1 does not defend c2 (c2 has no black defenders at all), which is why Rxc2 in the engine line wins it for nothing.

claims.quote: It is only a slight edge by comparison.
claims.why: Rgf1 is rated 103cp, which the scale puts in the clear/significant band (101-250), not slight.

claims.quote: White is fully developed.
claims.why: The bishop on c1 has not moved (the development list omits it, and the answer itself later calls Bb2 developing the last minor piece).

claims.quote: supporting d4
claims.why: From b2 the bishop does not defend d4 because White's own knight on c3 blocks the diagonal.

claims.quote: This retreats the bishop from the pin on f6
claims.why: There is no pin: e7 and d8 behind the f6 knight are empty, so the bishop on g5 pins nothing.

claims.quote: It brings the last undeveloped piece into the attack
claims.why: The knight is already developed on f3, while the rook on h1 is still on its starting square.

claims.quote: the offside knight is rerouted to b3
claims.why: Nb3 in the line is played by the knight from d4; the offside knight on a2 cannot reach b3 and stays on a2.

claims.quote: supports the e4 pawn first
claims.why: The bishop on e3 stands between e1 and e4, so a rook on e1 does not defend the e4 pawn.

claims.quote: It checks the king on d8
claims.why: A knight on c7 attacks a8, a6, b5, d5, e6 and e8, not d8, and the FACTS list no check for Nc7.

claims.quote: ends up 4 pawns ahead
claims.why: The 4 pawns is only the material gained during the line; Black already has queen, rook, bishop and two knights against rook and knight, so Black ends up far more than 4 pawns ahead.

claims.quote: White ends up two pawns ahead
claims.why: Black is currently up a piece and two pawns, so after White gains two pawns in the line Black is still ahead, not White.

claims.quote: Black's bishop on b4 pins the knight on c3 against the pawn on e4 and the king's side of the board.
claims.why: The knight on c3 is not pinned: White's pawn on d2 stands between it and the king on e1, and e4 is not on the bishop's line.

claims.quote: the queen on c8 eyes the h3 pawn
claims.why: The c8-h3 diagonal is blocked by Black's own pawn on e6, so the queen does not see h3.

claims.quote: Bf3 adds protection to d4
claims.why: A bishop on f3 does not attack or defend d4 (its diagonals run f3-e4-d5 and f3-e2-d1).

claims.quote: The line ends with Black five pawns ahead
claims.why: White starts 3 pawns ahead, so after Black wins a rook and knight for a bishop the board shows Black only 2 pawns ahead at the end.

claims.quote: White has to give up castling rights after the check
claims.why: After 9. d3 Qa5+ White can block with Bd2, Nc3, Nbd2, Nfd2, Qd2 or b4 and keep castling rights; Kf1 is not forced.

claims.quote: White picks up a pawn on b4 and ends one pawn ahead
claims.why: White is already up two knights for a pawn; at the end of the f6 line White is about 6 pawns ahead, not 1.

claims.quote: It trades queens and ends with White three pawns ahead
claims.why: At the end of the Qc5 line White has two rooks and a knight against a rook (about 8 pawns ahead), not 3.

claims.quote: It also trades queens, leaving White one pawn ahead
claims.why: At the end of the Qe5 line White is still up two knights (about 6 pawns ahead), not 1.
